newsitem.title: INDIA: India to ensure naphtha supplies to power firms.
newsitem.headline: India to ensure naphtha supplies to power firms.

text.p: Indian Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral on Tuesday asked government officials to ensure adequate supplies of naphtha to power producers and take steps to help generate an additional 40,000 megawatts of power in the ninth plan period (1997-2002).
"He directed the cabinet secretary to set up a group to ensure that all arrangements for delivery of naphtha supplies should be tied up within one month," an official spokesman told reporters.
The cabinet secretary is the highest ranking civil servant in the nation.
In November 1995, the Indian government allowed setting up of short gestation liquid fuel-based power plants to bridge the gap in power supply.
Fearing a shortage of naphtha, the government restricted fuel linkages for a power generation capacity of 12,000 megawatts.
Gujral was speaking at a presentation on energy sector by officials of the Planning Commission, the country apex planning body.

"He (Gujral) also directed that a meeting should be held with the Reserve Bank of India and other concerned agencies to ensure that power projects get the amount of credit required by them," the official spokesman said.
Gujral asked officials to lay down procedures within two weeks for clearing investment for renovation and upgradation of power plants.
